---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. Only two or more unresolved, mutually incompatible choices that change an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow form a product business ambiguity; block only the smallest affected modeling slice. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms are not product blockers. Contract discovery and reversible technical defaults are not substitutes for business facts.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`, frontend component contracts, or Runtime Client SDK assets. Shared Application Delivery still publishes the Runtime Client SDK for an independent frontend Skill; this Builder Skill never fetches, copies, installs, generates, validates, or takes ownership of it. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. One Host/Agent session and TODO own requirements → model → apply → implementation → verify → package → Runtime → canary → acceptance, including recoverable repair rounds. Follow every applicable routed reference. A light batch may omit only TODO sections allowed by the guide, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |
| loaded Skill, CLI identity, and normal command surface | [CLI identity and canonical command map](references/development-guide.md#cli-identity-and-canonical-command-map) |
| complete TODO, Gate first-execution receipts, and session ownership | [session TODO and Gate receipts](references/development-guide.md#session-todo-and-gate-receipts) |
| project ownership and frontend finding routing | [project and frontend boundaries](references/development-guide.md#project-and-frontend-boundaries) |
| requirements extraction and critical ambiguity | [requirements to domain facts](references/development-guide.md#requirements-to-domain-facts) |
| domain truth, settlement, list Report, and technical prevention Gates | [domain truth design](references/development-guide.md#domain-truth-design) |
| capability reconciliation and metadata modeling | [model and capability mapping](references/development-guide.md#model-and-capability-mapping) |
| declarative authoring and the only release command | [model apply is the only release](references/development-guide.md#model-apply-is-the-only-release) |
| bounded installed-batch Action context | [source prepare implementation packet](references/development-guide.md#source-prepare-implementation-packet) |
| valid check, source finalize, focused tests, and exact receipts | [project check to finalize to tests](references/development-guide.md#project-check-to-finalize-to-tests) |
| semantic journey binding and highest-risk canary | [semantic execution and canary](references/development-guide.md#semantic-execution-and-canary) |
| managed Runtime and exact-denominator acceptance | [Runtime and acceptance](references/development-guide.md#runtime-and-acceptance) |
| evidence ceiling and terminal states | [done terminal policy](references/development-guide.md#done-terminal-policy) |
| initial credential and acceptance-identity safety | [system seed login](references/development-guide.md#system-seed-login) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

Before resolving or resuming this continuation, prove the original Host/Agent turn has actually ended. An outer exec session reporting `Unknown process id`, missing its timing trailer, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence and must never trigger a concurrent Agent against the same session. The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

### Explicit post-apply source-finalization continuation

Use this distinct compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` after a fresh successful `model apply` materialization whose source finalization failed solely on generated project-owned Action placeholders, and the caller has completed those Action sources. It does not accept or alter the already-current `source-finalization-continuation` route.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile post-apply-source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

The resolver validates the current signed backend materialization and its exact machine failure receipt before creating state. That receipt must contain only the structured `project.source_placeholder_remains` diagnostics for Action source in the `backend_technical_contract` check; every independent preflight check must have passed, and only the dependent composition check may be skipped. The current source must be a placeholder-free, finalization-ready evolution of that receipt in which only project-owned `backend/actions/**` paths changed. Runtime Client SDK and frontend materialization receipts are never accepted.

On success the resolver atomically owns one TODO, Gate state, and profile with exactly three ordered one-shot recipes:

```text
project check --scope actions → project source finalize → focused Go test
```

Execute only the returned `run_recipes`. Do not edit, add, reorder, duplicate, reopen, attach evidence to, or invoke the underlying product commands outside the profile runner. Partial state, symlinks, traversal or unbounded package paths, changed materialization/failure/source/CLI identities, a forged receipt, any non-placeholder failure, terminal failure, or a different/extra Gate fails closed with no replacement TODO. A completed terminal profile returns no recipes and never reopens. Do **not** read the whole-project guide, TODO template, or another whole-project reference for this profile.

### Explicit project verification continuation

Use this compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-verification-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. It is independent from package continuation. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-verification-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint validates the current backend-only materialization, source finalization and identity, Runtime manifest, and backend Application Delivery binding. Python consumes that checkpoint and atomically owns any required one-Gate TODO/state/profile. If verification is already current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise execute the sole returned machine-owned `project verify --json` recipe exactly once. Never supply a label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or binding. Partial/conflicting/unsafe state, stale profile identity, receipt tampering, an extra or reordered Gate, a repeated terminal command, or a changed pre-execution checkpoint fails closed without replacement.

### Explicit project package continuation

Use this separate compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-package-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-package-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint requires the current V6 verification plus the same current backend binding/materialization/finalization/source/Runtime identity closure. If the package receipt is current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise it atomically owns one machine Gate and returns only the fixed `project package --json` recipe. Execute it exactly once; never author its label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or bindings. The same partial, conflict, symlink/traversal, stale/tamper, extra/reordered Gate, terminal-repeat, and pre-execution-change cases fail closed without overwriting state or accepting an older receipt.

### Explicit Runtime process continuation

Use this compact route when the caller asks only to recover the already-packaged managed Runtime start/status boundary. Use the current Host session ID for this fresh compact continuation; do not create or reuse a whole-project TODO for that session. It does not require loading the whole-project guide, verification references, TODO template, verification authorities, or Gate runner source. Resolve the machine-owned profile once:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile runtime-process-continuation \
  --runtime-address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>
```

When the session has no TODO, Gate state, or Runtime profile, the resolver atomically creates its canonical two-Gate minimal TODO, synchronized state, and profile. It owns the fixed labels, `runtime_start` → `runtime_status` kinds, Gate IDs, exact argv, source/Runtime/cohort bindings, current packaged bundle, packaged CLI, numeric loopback address, and all pinned identities. The tool guarantees that the actual listener is the requested loopback and records its proof; the Agent adds no bind command or listener check. Stdout is only the compact envelope with the remaining `run_recipes`; execute them in order. Do not supply or author a TODO, label, marker, Gate ID, bundle, command argv, or identity binding yourself. Re-resolve after start to obtain only the status recipe when recovering from compaction. A partial session, non-profile-owned TODO, symlink, extra/reordered/forged Gate, changed address/package/source/CLI identity, stale state, terminal failure, or conflict fails closed without deleting or overwriting caller state; a terminal Gate never reopens.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Repair model/input failures and rerun it through a new round-specific Gate in the same session TODO; never reopen a terminal Gate, split release steps, bypass review, or treat `--product-surfaces` as frontend authorization.
- Run each check, finalize, and focused test through its own Gate on first execution. The runner serializes the Gate across processes; a passed or failed receipt makes only that Gate terminal. `checkpoint`, `status`, and `--require-complete` are recovery evidence, not task-exit instructions. After repair, add a round-specific Gate to the same TODO, sync, rerun invalidated checks, and continue in the same Host/Agent session. Never rerun a terminal Gate or reuse another receipt.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success. For unchanged/replay record hashes, use `runtimeRecordDurableSnapshot` (or copied-harness `durable_record_snapshot`), never the whole HTTP response body.
- When a settled requirement explicitly names an initial/default field value, add one TODO checkpoint that records the requirement evidence, exact Object-field JSON Pointer, concrete `default_value`, and its matching option/state entry. Close it only after the pointer exists in the applied model and validation proves membership; never leave the behavior only in acceptance prose or infer a default from silence. The authoritative mapping and applied example are in [CRUD and state machine](references/capabilities/crud-and-state-machine.md).
- After finalization and focused tests pass, run the highest-risk semantic canary before broad Runtime integration. Failure makes dependents temporarily ineligible, never ends the task: repair its owner, add repair Gates to the same TODO, rerun invalidated checks, and continue without shrinking the model or denominator.
- Model validation, apply, source checks, verify, package, Runtime start/health, canary, and acceptance failures use the same bounded diagnose → owner repair → rerun loop. Keep all quality, safety, ownership, and denominator Gates; no compatibility layer, fallback, weaker oracle, excluded case, or reduced denominator. Stop only with exhausted evidence of unavailable required service/permission/credential, unresolvable result-changing ambiguity, data/security risk, or contradictory contracts.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repair inconsistency and rerun until it passes. This linter pass is not test, Runtime, delivery, or scenario evidence. Provide a concise completion summary with implemented scope, test results, Runtime results, and explicitly non-blocking limitations. ## System seed login Runtime owns every initial credential. Never write credential rows, embed a password in model/source/TODO/evidence, or replace formal provisioning and password-change flows. The canonical system identity is user ID `admin`, login `admin@example.com`, Admin Console `/admin`, Surface `admin_console`. # Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. The CLI-compiled capability disclosure and Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source and dependencies stay externally owned and read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [backend-runtime.md](backend-runtime.md) for the closed backend Runtime boundary. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → source implementation → verify → package → managed Runtime → semantic canary → acceptance → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. For normal whole-project work this entire chain, including repair rounds, stays in one Host/Agent session and one TODO. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` and `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` routes are selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. They never load this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; each compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. A non-zero status is a checkpoint showing what must be repaired; it never means exit, wait for the user, or open another session. Repair in this session, append round-specific Gates to this TODO for terminal failed commands, sync, rerun affected checks, and retry the checkpoint. Before any genuinely necessary Host resume after an unrecoverable interruption, first prove the original Agent turn has actually ended; an outer exec wrapper reporting `Unknown process id`, losing its timing output, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence. Never start a second Agent against the same session TODO/Gates while the first may still be alive. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. Normal recovery never changes this identity. A later session exists only after the original task was genuinely interrupted or externally blocked; it creates a new file and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Treat every round as bounded by its complete safely reachable finding inventory, one owner-grouped repair batch, and the invalidated checks it must rerun; repeat while findings remain. Ordinary non-zero results from model validation/apply, source checks, verify, package, Runtime start/health, canary, or acceptance are recoverable inputs to this loop, not an Agent/session boundary. Do not add a compatibility layer, fallback, weaker oracle, excluded case, or reduced denominator. Stop the whole task only after evidence proves one of four genuinely unrecoverable conditions: a required external service, permission, or credential remains unavailable after every authorized recovery path; two or more unresolved business choices would change a required observable result and no accepted authority permits a safe choice; continuation would risk data corruption or security; or governing contracts are objectively contradictory. Record the attempted recovery paths and their evidence. Otherwise remain in the same Host/Agent session and TODO, repair, rerun, and continue. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey temporarily ineligible for execution, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner in this session, add any terminal-command repair Gates to the same TODO, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks before automatically continuing. “Blocked” here prevents invalid downstream evidence; it never ends the Agent task. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Never retry mutations before this check, initialize an existing project without authorization, or create a nested repository inside another worktree. - Preserve the full requirement; do not silently reduce it to an MVP, demo, phase, or core subset. - Establish users, roles, goals, lifecycles, exceptional paths, and the complete operation inventory before modeling. - Apply industry business practices where they clarify the requested product without expanding its scope. - Before first backend publication, model local/test-only non-human acceptance identities, their formal login/session path, required Workforce profiles and assignments, departments/jobs/positions, business menu definitions, role-menu assignments, and the minimum real records for every acceptance journey. The implementer may add the minimum contrasting identities needed to prove same-record allow/deny, data-Scope, and requester isolation; these are acceptance fixtures, not evidence of the product's organization size or role cardinality. Do not defer these prerequisites to verify or seed online credentials. For an existing project: - Read current requirement documents, Git state, backend source, metadata, tests, and managed delivery state. - Record current behavior and the affected dependency closure in the TODO. - Plan only the requested increment and required regression coverage. - Retain valid existing source; do not rewrite it to manufacture workflow evidence. ## Initialization Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, session ID, TODO, compact `resume_packet`, one-time `authoring_context`, routed reference paths, and package identity to the result. `DOMAINRY_CLI` must equal the same package's single executable `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. Never resolve a CLI through `PATH`, substitute another Skill, or call Domainry Plane directly. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. These actions are setup rather than stages or TODO gates. Use only the applicable command families below, in TODO order. Add one pinned `--environment ` or `--service ` target wherever shown and keep it consistent. Use `--help` only to resolve listed-command flags; do not invent neighboring commands. # Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract; frontend dependency installation and package wiring are outside this Skill.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, BFF, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. Application-facing client selection and wiring belong to the frontend owner outside this Skill; Builder models only the Application Delivery-published `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}/run`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/records/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Backend acceptance wraps typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, Product Surface, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request (gate: G04). For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

For normal whole-project work, start and inspect the Runtime through separate managed Runtime start/status Gates in the current Host/Agent session TODO, using the packaged CLI, current project-relative bundle, and an explicit numeric loopback address such as `127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. The Gate runner validates the exact argv and source/Runtime/cohort bindings and requires the `domainry-managed-runtime-process-v3` response/receipt. A failed start or status Gate remains immutable evidence: diagnose it, repair the owner, append a uniquely labeled repair-round Gate pair to the same TODO, sync, rerun, and continue. Neither Gate closes the broader acceptance-session and differentiated-data readiness item.

Use the machine-owned `runtime-process-continuation` profile only for a caller-explicit standalone recovery after an earlier Agent task has ended. Its compact TODO and returned recipes are not the normal whole-project phase transition. Stop with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project <project>` after acceptance. The managed receipt records the address, so subsequent acceptance commands use the same Runtime cohort. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or assemble Runtime Gate controls by hand.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Stop Runtime and reclaim ports and processes after scenarios. A running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `project source finalize`, compile, tests, and `project check` do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `project source finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) or recursive call cycle — do pure selection into bounded slices and call the generated batch/query capability once outside the loop; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Generated batch inputs are 1 through 200, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal accepted fan-out shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `project verify` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** A `conditional_update` Handler mutation without a compare-and-set token or predicate fails at runtime with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. Attach the condition observed under `GetForUpdate`:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)` predicates and `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)` are the generated condition surface (arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects are inherently compare-and-set and also satisfy the requirement). On idempotent replay the predicate legitimately differs (equal-to-current instead of null); test assertions must compare per-execution expected mutations, not demand identical mutations.

The generated data package exports `ValidateConditionalMutation`, and both the real data layer and the scaffolded fakes enforce it — a mutation with no condition fails unit tests with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. A hand-written fake must route through the same helper; never write one that accepts an unconditional mutation. As a cheap belt-and-suspenders guard for call sites no unit case exercises, after implementing each module and before `project source finalize`, run the static self-check from the project root and require exit code 0 (`grep -L` alone does not encode the verdict in its exit status, so the wrapper below is the command to bind as Gate evidence):

```bash
bash -c 'viol=$(grep -rl --include="*.go" -e ".ConditionalUpdate(" backend | grep -v "/generated/" | grep -v "_test\.go" | xargs -r grep -LE "Require[A-Za-z]+\(|WithExpectedUpdatedAt\(|Increment[A-Za-z]*\(|Decrement[A-Za-z]*\("); [ -z "$viol" ] || { echo "$viol"; exit 1; }'
```

Exit 1 lists every file that builds a `ConditionalUpdate` with no condition anywhere in that file; each will fail live with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. The check is file-granular: a file that mixes one conditioned and one bare call still passes, so keep one handler per file (the default layout). The development TODO template carries this as a required implementation-stage checkbox — bind it with `... run <gate-id> --bind source --` followed by the command above verbatim (it already starts with `bash -c`).

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.
# Domain truth and settlement

## Gate

Freeze business facts before capability discovery. Platform capabilities decide how accepted facts map to Runtime; they do not decide what the facts are.

| Kind | Meaning | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Occurred fact | A completed business event and its event-time inputs, rules, and result | Persist when it occurs; correct by reversal or adjustment |
| Summary | A read-only aggregation of occurred facts | Use Dataset or native SQL; never own the formula that created the fact |
| Simulation | A hypothetical result under assumed inputs or rules | Isolate from official facts, ledgers, payroll, and reports |

For every material calculation, decide: Calculation Owner, Evaluation Time, Persisted Result, Policy/Rule Snapshot, Input Snapshot, Calculation Trace, Correction/Reversal Strategy, Downstream Consumers, and Report Source of Truth. Keep only the smallest affected modeling slice blocked when accepted evidence leaves at least two incompatible choices that change the explicitly required formula, amount/unit semantics, occurred-fact identity, correction behavior, or observable result. Exact decimal representation, a stated threshold, and summation remain modelable when optional currency, unit, or range metadata is absent; use nullable metadata and stated command preconditions, and do not invent conversion rules. Route Runtime-owned representations through contract discovery and reversible persistence, index, audit, idempotency, and concurrency mechanics through the `safe_implementation_decision` rule in [development-guide.md](development-guide.md#requirements-to-domain-facts); those choices do not become product business ambiguity, but their later verification remains mandatory.

## Versioned settlement pattern

```text
Versioned Policy
  → Atomic Settlement Action
  → Calculation Snapshot
  → Immutable Ledger
  → Reversal / Adjustment
  → Native SQL Report
  → Server-paginated Consumers
  → Same-Report bounded threshold router (sync exhausted <=1000 / async on row 1001)
  → Async Terminal Notification
  → Payroll / Export Reconciliation
```

Use this pattern for an event that locks money, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll input. In one transaction, the settlement Action must validate idempotency and authorization, resolve the event-time policy, and persist policy identity/version, the actual rule snapshot, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, final result, immutable ledger entries, and audit/outbox effects. A later policy version affects only later events.

Never update or delete an original financial ledger entry to correct history. Append a linked reversal for cancellation/refund and a reasoned adjustment for an approved correction. Preserve `reversal_of` or equivalent lineage, the original ledger ID, actor, time, reason, and approval boundary. A locked payroll/export consumer records the ledger IDs or a governed scope/hash it consumed; later adjustments follow the explicit correction period instead of silently changing the locked result.

## Anti-patterns

- Repeating one formula across pages or several reports.
- Joining current Settings to recompute a historical financial result.
- Rendering absent or unproven facts as numeric zero.
- Giving summary, detail, page, payroll, and export different scopes or formulas.
- Allowing Settings changes to drift historical results.
- Omitting ledger-ID-level traceability across consumers.
- Building a project-specific report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator.
- Returning an unbounded list or fetching all rows for browser-memory pagination.
- Bypassing the fixed 1000-row router, using a second export-only query, or producing duplicate artifacts for an equivalent canonical fingerprint.
- Completing or failing an export without a notification linked to its audit, job, and artifact, or allowing an unaudited/unexpired-but-out-of-scope download.

## Acceptance matrix

Cover applicable boundaries with event-time input, policy identity, snapshot/ledger IDs, trace, consumer result, and allow/deny evidence:

- policy version switch before/after effective time;
- business-day cutoff and cross-midnight events;
- multi-party allocation with deterministic remainder handling;
- full/partial refund and reversal lineage;
- correction after payroll or another consumer is locked;
- summary/detail/page/payroll/export reconciliation by ledger ID;
- cross-store and cross-entity permission/data-scope denial;
- Runtime restart and Settings change without historical drift.
- maximum-page enforcement and stable cursor traversal without duplicate or missing rows, including equal sort keys;
- explicit `truncated` and exact/estimated/omitted `total` semantics;
- exact permission-filtered totals at 0, 1000, and 1001 with synchronous/asynchronous routing and identical Report/parameters/source/Scope;
- concurrent, running, completed, expired, failed/cancelled, source-change and Scope-change fingerprint replay semantics;
- asynchronous completed and failed terminal notifications linked to export audit/job/artifact, plus requester/Scope/expiry/integrity/audit download denial.
# Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the backend metadata inventory and source of truth; `backend/reports/*.sql` is the source-owned SQL surface referenced by Report model items. The Blueprint Ledger under `domain/` and everything under `.domainry/` are CLI-owned projections that `model apply` converges from those sources. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**` by hand, and never treat them as an authoring input.

## File contract

Every file under `backend/model/` matching `*.json` is loaded, in lexical filename order:

```json
{
  "contract_version": "domainry-backend-model-v1",
  "items": [
    {
      "module": "project",
      "kind": "project",
      "key": "project",
      "payload": {"blueprint": {"schema_version": "1", "id": "gym", "name": "Gym", "description": "Gym operations"}}
    },
    {
      "module": "membership",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "key": "membership-management",
      "depends_on": ["project/project/project"],
      "payload": {"requirement": {"statement": "Manage membership metadata", "acceptance_criteria": ["Membership metadata validates"], "behaviors": [], "no_executable_behavior_reason": "This minimal file-contract example emits no executable resource"}}
    },
    {
      "module": "membership",
      "kind": "actor_role",
      "key": "membership-roles",
      "requirement_keys": ["membership-management"],
      "depends_on": ["project/project/project", "membership/requirement/membership-management"],
      "payload": {"emits": [{"collection": "roles", "key": "membership_member", "value": {"key": "membership_member", "name": "Membership member", "permissions": [], "record_scope": "all_records"}}]}
    }
  ]
}
```

Item fields:

- `module`, `kind`, `key` — required identity. `kind` is one of `project`, `requirement`, `actor_role`, `object_relation`, `action_authorization`, `workflow_connector`, `acceptance`, `resource`. Identity segments are stable lowercase keys; the unique project item is always `project/project/project`.
- `status` — optional, `closed` (default) or `decision_required`; `decision_required` must match at least one unresolved decision.
- `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, `decisions` — optional arrays (default empty). `depends_on` entries are full `module/kind/key` addresses.
- `payload` — the item body (default `{}`), identical to the Ledger item payload contract for that kind.

One `module/kind/key` may be declared exactly once across all model files. Group items by owning module — typically one file per module (`backend/model/<module>.json`). Do not add envelope fields (`contract_version`, `module`, `kind`, `key`) inside `payload`, and do not nest `status`, `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, or `decisions` there.

## Requirement payload

A `requirement` item's `payload.requirement` carries the requirement statement plus its `behaviors[]` array of behavior-owner tuples (owner, resource_key, and the tuple fields defined in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md)). An empty `behaviors` array is legal only when the payload also supplies a non-empty `no_executable_behavior_reason` string explaining why the requirement owns no executable behavior (for example, purely declarative authorization/navigation policy carried by roles, data permissions, and views). The field must be absent when `behaviors` is non-empty; `model validate` fails closed on both violations (`empty behaviors require a reason` / `ledger.requirement_incomplete`).

For `object_sql_v1`, use exactly one project-owned SQL file named after the Report key instead of embedding a large escaped SQL string. Replace only the `sql` member with `"sql_file":"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"`. `model validate|plan|apply` requires that exact canonical project-relative regular file, rejects symlinks/traversal and simultaneous `sql` + `sql_file`, normalizes line endings and a final newline, records its SHA-256 in the apply receipt, and embeds the normalized SQL into the existing published Runtime contract. `sql_file` is not a Runtime field or a query DSL; Runtime still receives `object_sql_v1.sql`, and `model export` may therefore emit the compatible inline form.

## Commands

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model preflight        --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan     --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply    --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [--environment <name> | --service <url>] [--allow-destructive] [--sync-only] [--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export   --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--force]
```

- `preflight` is the authoritative no-HTTP, local-read-only repair loop. It reuses the same model/SQL loader, strict item contract, Ledger graph, in-process authoring checks, deterministic Project Contract projector, and Runtime-manifest compiler as the formal path. It atomically replaces `.domainry/builder/disposable/model-preflight-result.json` for both `valid` and `repair_required`; stdout contains only `state`, `issue_count`, the project-relative artifact locator, SHA-256, and identity. A repair result exits non-zero. Read the artifact from the first Gate run and batch-repair it; do not rerun a failed Gate merely to obtain diagnostics and do not implement a bespoke `jq`/regex preflight. This local boundary does not claim live Plane, Runtime configuration, provider, database, or scenario checks.
- `validate` parses every model file, enforces the item contract, and reports the pending plan counts without writing model/Ledger state.
- `plan` additionally lists the exact item IDs classified as create, update, or delete.
- `apply` is the single release command: it converges the Ledger to the model files, gates on the aggregated metadata checklist, then chains live validation, signed publication, dependency resolution, backend materialization/evolution, and source finalization, stopping at the first failing stage. Every release apply resolves the dependency seed in staging before it installs files or writes a successful materialization receipt; a resolution failure stops closed and must be repaired before another round. For an existing Builder delivery change, the first run emits `evolution_review_required` plus an audit path and SHA-256. Inspect the immutable audit and run the same product command through a new round-specific Gate with that exact emitted SHA-256 and a concrete review reason; never calculate or substitute the hash. After any other failure, repair the model files (or the reported stage input) and use a new Gate for the next command run. stdout carries one compact summary; the complete receipt is written to `.domainry/builder/model-apply.json`. `--sync-only` stops after the Ledger sync and checklist for local iteration without a Domainry Plane target.
- `export` bootstraps model files from the current Ledger (one file per module) for a project created before this workflow; it refuses to overwrite existing model files without `--force`.

CAS identities, batch contexts, and Ledger journals are handled entirely inside the CLI. Never compute, copy, or supply a SHA-256 by hand, and never call Domainry Plane directly or reconstruct its request signing.

## Convergence and safety rules

`plan`/`apply` classify every declared item against the current Ledger:

- **create / update** — applied automatically and atomically; an unchanged item is never rewritten.
- **delete** — an item present in the Ledger but absent from the model is destructive. `apply` refuses and names the missing items until the model restores them or the run explicitly passes `--allow-destructive`.
- A **rename** of `module`, `kind`, or `key` is a delete plus a create. Treat renames as destructive: confirm data expectations first, then apply with explicit consent.
- The model owns definitions only. Runtime instance data — business records, sessions, credentials, user-role assignments made at runtime — is never compared or mutated by convergence.

Complete each module's full inventory (Objects, Relations, Actions, Roles, authorization, data scopes, Workflows, state machines, Reports, Schedulers, Automations, Connectors, seeds, acceptance) before the first `model validate`; do not validate a partial inventory and do not use `validate` or `apply` as a resource-by-resource schema probe. Immediately before the first validation, perform one cross-resource preflight over the whole draft: ownership closes **both ways** (every requirement behavior resolves to its resource, and every emitted Action/Workflow/Scheduler/Automation — including export/audit helper Actions — has one matching behavior owner); every Action's allowed roles have the required object access plus reads of every declared project relation target; Identity bootstrap/demo-user/profile references resolve; every frontend entrypoint object exists; Report SQL paths equal `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`; export controls resolve their Report, Action, audit/download Objects, mappings, and one role's complete grant chain; every declared Object has a valid seed; and acceptance actors, roles, operations, positive cases, and denial cases resolve. Run validation only after this inventory is closed. On failure, collect and repair the complete diagnostic set and re-run once; do not revalidate after each local edit. Once validation returns `state:"valid"`, keep that model immutable while attaching evidence. Any requirement-backed edit invalidates the result and starts a new atomic `validate` + `plan` cycle. After a failed apply, fix the complete finding set in the files and re-run once.

**Initial/default-state closure is part of that single preflight.** For every explicit requirement or accepted evidence statement that names an initial or default field value, author the value as the owning `objects[].fields[].default_value`. This is mandatory when the Object is exposed through generic Runtime create (including `entrypoints[].create_objects` or a role's `<object>.create` permission); acceptance prose, a seed, a frontend form default, or an Action input constant is not metadata default behavior. Mechanically verify that every select default matches its stable field option vocabulary and every state-field default matches both that vocabulary and the owning `state_machines[].states`. If the requirement does not identify an initial/default value, do not invent one merely to satisfy prose; record only the deterministic behavior the accepted demand actually establishes.

Before that first validation, apply this strict nested-shape card; these objects reject aliases and convenient prose fields:

- `identity_bootstrap.menus[]` uses `id`, `key`, `label`, optional `description`/`route`/`icon`/`parent_id`, and required `sort_order` plus `status`; there is no `surface`. Bind roles with one row per pair, `role_menus:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]`, or with `role_menu_sets:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_ids":["menu_my_work"]}]`; never use `role_key`, `menu_keys`, or a grouped object under `role_menus`.
- Object field `validation` uses the exact Blueprint keys `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `options`, and `target`; `minimum`/`maximum` are Runtime authoring API names, not Blueprint JSON fields.
- Every `expected_reports[].metrics` value is an array; use `[]` when the scenario asserts execution/export but no metric values. It is never an object map.
- A Report emission repeats its identity inside the value: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`. The envelope `key` does not populate `value.key`; omitting the inner key makes `sql_file` resolve against an empty report key. The two keys must be identical.
- For `object_sql_v1`, each SQL `JOIN ... AS <alias>` has exactly one `join_cardinalities` entry shaped `{"alias":"<alias>","cardinality":"many_to_one"}` (or another truthful supported cardinality). It has only `alias` and `cardinality`; never use `left_alias`/`right_alias` there. Those names belong to Dataset join definitions, not Object SQL cardinality declarations.
- `report_export_controls[]` is closed to the fields listed in [reports](capabilities/reports.md). Do not invent requester/scope convenience properties; requester scoping is enforced by the declared grant chain and record mapping.
- `object_sql_v1` SQL has explicit `ORDER BY` and a literal business-bounded `LIMIT` in the inclusive range `1..10000`; the Blueprint `limit` diagnostic refers to SQL text, not a JSON `limit` property. Never use a larger placeholder such as `LIMIT 100000`.

Business menu definitions and role-menu assignments are **not emitted collections**. They are deterministic project bootstrap facts under the single project-level `identity_bootstrap` object. When acceptance names `effective_menu_list`, declare the needed `identity_bootstrap.menus` and either `role_menus` or `role_menu_sets` before apply; authoring rejects a probed role with no binding. Do not postpone that acceptance prerequisite to a manual post-apply step. Runtime's Identity menu management API remains the supported path for later operational edits; updates keep their normal schema-hash CAS contract.

`identity_bootstrap` (departments, organization scopes/memberships, workforce profiles/assignments, menus and role-menu bindings) is **not** an emits collection — an emitted collection always renders as an array and fails `schema.type: expected object`. It is a single project-level Blueprint property: declare it inside the **project item's `payload.blueprint.identity_bootstrap`** as `{"version":"1","departments":[{"id":"east","name":"East"}],"menus":[{"id":"menu_my_work","key":"my_work","label":"My work","route":"business.my_work","sort_order":10,"status":"active"}],"role_menus":[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]}`. `version` is the **string** constant `"1"` (integer `1` fails `schema.const`). `demo_users[].department_id` must reference a department `id` declared there (`identity.user_department_not_found` otherwise).

`demo_users[].profile_bindings` is the single owner of a demo user's business-profile link. Its referenced profile seed must leave the profile extension's `identity_relation_field` absent; do not also write a user ID into that seed field. `model validate` rejects the two-owner form as `identity.user_profile_seed_relation_owned_twice`, before Runtime bootstrap. Runtime still converges the exact pre-existing same-user link idempotently for older valid deliveries, but a different-user replacement remains a conflict.

Two more Action/role rules the validator enforces:

- **Every project-owned Handler Action — including scheduler-driven bulk handlers — must declare at least one required payload field in `idempotency_keys`** (`ledger.action_idempotency_required`). A scheduled job's invocation payload carries the key (e.g. a required `run_date` bound from the trigger event).
- **Multiple `data_permissions[]` entries for the same object do NOT merge**: the validator reads one entry's `read`/`write` per object, so "read=department + write=own" cannot be expressed as two entries (`ledger.action_role_data_permission_required` reports the losing entry's booleans). Declare a single entry with the union capability and enforce the narrower write constraint through a before-update automation assert on the owner, a Handler precondition, or CRUD permission removal.

## Single ownership

Every rendered resource key has exactly one originating model item. A `ledger.resource_duplicate` diagnostic means a second item attempted to emit an existing resource; it is never an overlay or merge mechanism. Repair it in the model files: remove the duplicate declaration and extend the item that already owns the resource. For example, a missing permission on an emitted role belongs in the item that already emits the role, not in a new `actor_role` item emitting the same role key.

Every behavior `resource_key` must resolve to the concrete resource owned by that behavior; the exact owner-to-emitted-collection mapping and resource-key rules live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md) — do not guess a collection from prose.

Agent metadata is resource-owned in the same model: emit `skills`, `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `agent_service_principals`, and `agent_entrypoints` from separate `resource` items in dependency order, each linked to the requirement it satisfies. Never place these collections inside the project item. Read [Agents and Agent Tasks](capabilities/agents-and-agent-tasks.md) before authoring them; exact fields and references come from the live Blueprint Definition consumed by `model validate|plan|apply`.

## Action declarations

An emitted `actions[]` entry requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `kind`, and `audit_event`. `kind` is the closed enum `bulk_operation`, `conditional_update`, `object_create`, `object_operation`, `record_delete`, `record_operation`, `record_restore`, `record_update`, or `transition_state`.

**Kind selection for Handler Actions**: a project-owned Handler must NOT use kind `object_create` — that kind carries the system `record.create` owner, and an Action with both a system operation and a business handler owner is rejected at **Runtime bootstrap** ("action has both system operation record.create and business handler owners"); no static stage (validate/finalize/check/verify/package) catches it. Use **`object_operation`** for an object-level Handler command (creation included) and **`record_operation`** for a record-targeted one; a Handler that creates records does the create through its data capabilities.

Authorization splits by ownership and both halves are enforced at compile time (`ledger.runtime_manifest_invalid`):

- A **project-owned Handler Action** (one that declares `handler`) uses the `authorization` block (`allowed_roles`, …).
- A **system Action** (`transition_state` and every other non-Handler kind) must instead declare `permission` — it compiles to Runtime `requires_permission`. `authorization` is rejected on a system Action, and a missing `permission` is rejected too. Runtime executes a system Action for any role holding that permission, so a role that must not execute a guarded transition (for example, "only managers close") must not hold the declared permission — or the transition must be owned by a manager-only Handler Action instead.
- **The `permission` key must be exactly two dot-segments: `<object_key>.<suffix>`** (e.g. `ticket.transition_close`, not `ticket.transition.close`). Runtime authorization re-derives the check as `<action.object_key>.<last-segment>`, so a three-segment key like `ticket.transition.start` passes `model validate` and one authorization layer but is re-read as the never-granted `ticket.start` by the second — every legitimate caller then fails with 403 `backend.permission.denied` at runtime. Platform permission keys granted verbatim in `roles[].permissions` (e.g. `identity.audit.view`) are exact-match strings and are not subject to this rule; it binds project-declared Action `permission` values and object CRUD keys.

Acceptance scenarios are strict Blueprint resources, not free-form test notes. Use only the declared top-level fields `key`, `name`, `description`, `actor`, `role`, `role_key`, `seed_data`, `seed_records`, `actions`, `attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_outcome`, `expected_error_code`, `expected_records`, `expected_reports`, `assertions`, and `config`; never invent shortcuts such as `objects` or `attempted_objects`. Express record/RLS expectations through `expected_records` or typed `assertions`.

`workflows` means a positive **manual** Workflow invocation and therefore requires `trigger_contract.type:"manual"`. Do not list `scheduled`, `action_completed`, or `record_event` Workflows there: the finalizer attributes them to their real trigger owner (the matching `scheduled_jobs`, Action, or Automation operation) and rejects a fabricated manual-run case with `acceptance.workflow_manual_trigger_required`.

The scenario-level `expected_outcome` closed enum is `""`, `positive`, `exception`, or `denied` — nothing else. Use `positive` for an expected success, `denied` for an expected Runtime authorization denial, and `exception` for every other expected non-success (state-machine rejection, RLS concealment, business precondition failure). Do not confuse it with the different `config.runtime_operations[].expected_outcome` enum documented below; the two enums are validated independently and values are not interchangeable. A `denied` scenario's role must actually be unable to execute every attempted Action: the composer rejects a denied scenario whose role holds the Action's authorization (`compose.acceptance_denied_role_can_execute_action`) — pick a genuinely unauthorized role or remove the grant.

### Acceptance composition rules enforced by `project acceptance prepare`

The denominator builder enforces these composition rules; authoring scenarios without them costs one repair round each:

- **Requirement coverage**: every `requirement` item — including purely declarative ones such as acceptance provisioning or navigation — must be reachable from at least one `acceptance` item's `requirement_keys` whose scenarios produce executable cases (`acceptance.requirement_coverage_missing: <key> resources=N operations=0 cases=0` otherwise). Cases come only from `actions`/`attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_reports`, and `config.runtime_operations`; a scenario carrying only `expected_records` produces no case.
- **Write denial coverage**: every write operation — each write Action and each write `runtime_operations` route — needs a denied-role case (`acceptance.permission_denial_missing`). For Actions, author a `denied` scenario with an unauthorized role. For typed routes, author a scenario whose `runtime_operations` entry sets **`"case": "permission_denied"`** (setting only `expected_outcome: denied` is not recognized); its default error code is `auth.permission_denied`, and its role must genuinely lack the route's required permissions.
- **Handler positive coverage is symmetric and DIRECT**: every Handler Action also needs a positive scenario whose `actions` list references it directly with an allowed role (`ledger.action_positive_scenario_missing`). Coverage through a Workflow branch that invokes the Handler does not count — a scheduler-driven or approval-driven Handler still needs one direct positive probe (e.g. the operator role invoking it with an explicit payload).
- **Every declared Object needs at least one seed** — including runtime-product objects such as reminder records or export audit/download artifacts (`ledger.seed_evidence_incomplete` names the missing objects); there is no exemption for objects normally populated only at runtime.
- Treat seed records as a closed typed graph before apply: every required field needs a value or declared default, every `$record:<seed-key>` relation must target a seed of the relation's declared object, option values must belong to the field value domain, and undeclared fields are errors. `model validate` reports these at the exact seed field; do not defer them to Runtime bootstrap.
- **Relation-typed `payload_fields` require `target_object_key`** referencing a **project** object; a Foundation target (e.g. an organization unit) is not resolvable there — pass the identifier as `text` and keep the Object field itself as the real relation.
